findings.message: Instance fix. The fix drops rolled-back rows one at a time, but it does not ask what each environment's latest deployment was. The Releases screen and listReleases (queries.ts:233) take `distinct on (release_id, environment_id) ... order by at desc`, so an environment whose latest deployment was rolled back shows as Rolled back there. The portfolio still finds the older 'deployed' row in that environment and reports the release as there. Fix: pick the latest non-voided deployment per environment first, keep only those with status deployed or testing, then take the highest position. Add this case to the table test.
findings.scenario: v1.1.0: deployed to QA, deployed to UAT at t1, then rolled back in UAT at t2 → the AMX row says 'in UAT', while the Releases page shows UAT Rolled back and the release is really in QA.

findings.message: A second copy of 'which environment is a release in now'. queries.ts:233 decides it by the latest deployment per environment; this subquery decides it with its own rule (any non-voided, non-rolled-back row). The two copies already disagree in the scenario above. Fix: derive the stage from the same latest-per-environment rule, ideally one shared SQL fragment, as in-prod.ts does for the In Prod rule.
findings.scenario: Same data as above: the Releases page and the portfolio row show different current environments for the same release.

findings.message: The superseded-release fix went into portfolio.ts only. The pin offer's 'newest release of the project not yet live in Prod' (pin-offers.ts:83-86) uses the same rule and has the same defect. Once the newer release is live, the older superseded one becomes the release a verified proposal is offered to join. The two now also disagree with each other: the portfolio says '1 verified / not released' while the pin offers the dead release. Fix: apply the same `created_at >` newest live-Prod release filter there, from one shared fragment.
findings.scenario: AFX: v1.0.0 never promoted, v1.0.5 live in Prod, AFX-001 verified with no release → the portfolio shows '1 verified, not released', but AFX-001's pin offers 'Put AFX-001 in AFX v1.0.0'.

findings.message: LAST_PROGRESS falls back to `p.created_at`. Migration 0012 left that column null for every proposal made before it ('not known'). For those proposals with no done task, LAST_PROGRESS is null, `null <= staleBefore` is null, and the stuck build reads as on-track. 'Could not tell when it last moved' is shown as 'clear'. Fix: treat a null last-progress time as unknown. Flag it, or fall back to a known timestamp, and don't drop it from the stale check silently. Add the null case to the AC-3 table.
findings.scenario: A building proposal created before migration 0012 (created_at null) with no tasks ticked, untouched for months → health on-track, healthReason null.

findings.message: The at-risk clock ignores phase changes. A proposal that spent weeks in planned and moved to building today, with no task done yet, is measured from its created_at. The project goes at-risk with 'unchanged for 14+ days' on the day work starts. The previous finding's suggested fix named a phase-change time; the clock should count the move into building as progress, through a recorded phase-change timestamp or the activity record of the move.
findings.scenario: AFX-003 created 2026-10-01 as planned, moved to building on 2026-11-20 with 0/5 tasks done → the AMX row shows at-risk, 'AFX-003 unchanged for 14+ days'.
